## The five analysts {#the-five-analysts}

```{r}
#| label: five-analysts
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.2
# The published result and the five reanalyses (data/reference_marks.csv,
# with the choices from data/analysts5.csv), each placed by its gap in points;
# the shaded band is the range of the curve of the claim.
choices <- datawizard::data_select(analysts, c("id", "comparison", "population"))
five <- marks |>
  dplyr::left_join(choices, by = "id") |>
  datawizard::data_modify(
    comparison = dplyr::coalesce(comparison, "Hispanic vs white names"),
    population = dplyr::coalesce(population, "replies"),
    lab = paste0(tag, "   ", sub("^Hispanic vs ", "against ", comparison), ", ", population),
    oa = id == "OA"
  ) |>
  datawizard::data_arrange("-b_pp") |>
  datawizard::data_modify(lab = factor(lab, levels = lab))

ggplot2::ggplot(five, ggplot2::aes(b_pp, lab)) +
  ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = min(curve$b_pp), xmax = max(curve$b_pp), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#d6dde5", alpha = 0.6) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = grey_mid, linewidth = 0.4) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = oa), size = 5.5) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = fmt_num(b_pp, 1)), hjust = -0.6, size = 5, colour = ink) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = ncl_blue, `TRUE` = burgundy), guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-24, 2), labels = \(x) fmt_num(x, 0)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Hispanic minus comparison names (points); shaded: the range of the curve",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_slide(15) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey20"))
```

::: {.small}
Every gap points the way of the claim, from `r fmt_num(min(five$b_pp), 1)` to `r fmt_num(max(five$b_pp), 1)` points, and every test is significant. Task 1 verdicts in the robustness study: `r sum(analysts$task1 == "evidence for the claim")` × evidence for the claim, `r sum(analysts$task1 == "no evidence either way")` × no evidence either way.
:::

::: notes
Here are the five, with the published result of the original authors in burgundy, each placed by its gap in percentage points. On direction everybody agrees, since every gap is negative and every test is significant, while the size runs from twenty points down to thirteen. UYV3F, P9W8Y and the published result compare the Hispanic with the white names among the replies and land at twenty, and EWFMI does the same with covariates and lands close by. 8PTRZ compares the Hispanic names with all the other names and lands at seventeen, because the Black names were greeted by name less often than the white ones. 25N5D counts every delivered email, a choice whose reason the causal graph makes clear, and lands at thirteen. The shaded band is the range of every specification fitted in the workshop.
:::

## What the five analysts did {#five-questions-two-verdicts .smaller}

```{r}
#| label: five-table
#| output: asis
# The five reanalyses as a Markdown table, from data/analysts5.csv.
stat_txt <- \(type, x) dplyr::case_when(
  is.na(x) ~ "none recorded",
  type == "chi2" ~ paste0("$\\chi^2$ = ", fmt_num(x, 3)),
  .default = paste0("*", type, "* = ", fmt_num(x, 3))
)
rows <- analysts |>
  datawizard::data_modify(line = paste0("| ", id, " | ", sub("^Hispanic vs ", "", comparison), " | ", population,
                                        " | ", method, " | ", stat_txt(statistic_type, statistic_recorded),
                                        " | ", task1, " |")) |>
  datawizard::data_extract("line")
cat(c("::: {.fs-60}",
      "| Analyst | Compared with | Emails counted | Method | Recorded | Verdict |",
      "|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|:--|",
      rows, ":::"), sep = "\n")
```

::: {.fragment .small}
Both verdicts of no evidence come from analysts whose own work shows a significant gap. 25N5D concluded that the effect was real but "substantially smaller than that reported in the original results"; the Task 1 model of P9W8Y in the robustness study tested ethnicity among the female names only.
:::

::: notes
Two analysts compare the Hispanic names with the white names only, as the claim was selected, one with the white and Black names together, as the abstract has it, and two fit all three groups at once, EWFMI to read off the contrast with the white names and P9W8Y to test whether the three groups differ at all. Four count the replies, and one counts every delivered email. [advance] Three concluded that the data were evidence for the claim, and two recorded no evidence either way, although the work of both shows a significant gap. 25N5D wrote that the effect was real, "though the magnitude of the effect is substantially smaller than that reported in the original results", so that verdict seems to judge the claim by the twenty points that the selected claim had dropped. The first model of P9W8Y included an interaction, so its test of ethnicity compared the female names alone, arguably a narrower test than the analyst intended.
:::
